title: 1987 AHSME Problem 23
statement: If \(p\) is a prime and both roots of \(x^2+px-444p=0\) are integers, then

solutions.text:
An integer root satisfies \[ x^2=p(444-x). \] Thus \(x\) is divisible by \(p,\) so write \(x=np.\) Substitution gives \[ n(n+1)p=444=2^2\cdot3\cdot37. \] The consecutive product condition works only with \(p=37,\) for which \(n=3\) or \(-4.\) The roots are \(111\) and \(-148,\) so \(31\lt p\le41.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: For an integer root \(x,\) rewrite the equation as \(x^2=p(444-x)\)
Since \(p\) is prime, write \(x=np\) and factor \(444\)
